description: In docker/docker-compose.yml the Realtime service sets DB_ENC_KEY to the literal string 'supabaserealtime' rather than interpolating from .env like every adjacent secret. The variable is absent from .env.example and untouched by generate-keys.sh, so users who follow the documented secret-rotation guidance still ship the public default. Realtime uses this key to AES-encrypt tenant database credentials (including the Postgres password) stored in the _realtime schema. An attacker who can read those tables — via backup leak, read-only SQLi, or misconfigured role — can decrypt the credentials offline and escalate to full database control.
reproduction: 1. Obtain read access to _realtime.extensions / _realtime.tenants (backup dump, SQLi, or over-privileged role)
2. Extract the AES-encrypted tenant database credential fields
3. Decrypt them offline using the publicly-known key 'supabaserealtime'
4. Use the recovered Postgres superuser password to authenticate with full privileges
technical_details: DB_ENC_KEY is assigned a fixed literal instead of a ${VAR} reference, and no generation/override path exists in .env.example or generate-keys.sh. Because the key is public in the repository, the AES encryption applied to tenant credentials in the _realtime schema provides no confidentiality against anyone who can read the ciphertext.
title: Hardcoded Realtime tenant-credential encryption key with no override
